subject: Cluster commitment pathway and ramping options for Pegasus Bio
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@pegasusbio.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity - initial sizing ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks promising for our customer-facing inference use cases. We are starting to map internal procurement timelines and need a clean set of committed options we can show our finance and infra teams.

High level ask: can you send 2–3 commitment profiles that map to (a) low-cost pilot, (b) predictable production baseline, (c) aggressive growth plan? For each profile we need: cluster size (GPUs), minimum guaranteed GPUs, burst/elasticity behavior, ramp schedule (weeks/months), and a top-level estimated monthly committed cost + delta if we enable autoscaling.

Attached is a short requirements sheet from our infra team (pegasus_requirements.xlsx).

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Patel
Head of ML Platforms, Pegasus Bio
asha@pegasusbio.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@pegasusbio.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - initial sizing ask

Hi Asha — great talking yesterday. Attached is a concise set of commitment profiles and a short pilot scope (proposed_terms.pdf, pilot_scope.docx). Below is a summarized, actionable set you can drop into finance slides.

Summary (high level estimates, USD/month committed):
- Option A: Pilot (cost-conscious)
  - Cluster: 4x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs
  - Min guaranteed: 2 GPUs
  - Burst: up to 12 GPUs via short-term burst pool (best-effort)
  - Ramp: 0 -> 2 in week 1; optional 2 -> 4 after pilot review (weeks 3–6)
  - Est. committed cost: $18,500/mo; autoscaling add-on +$2,200/mo (approx)

- Option B: Production baseline (predictable)
  - Cluster: 16x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (sharded across 2 nodes)
  - Min guaranteed: 12 GPUs (SLA-backed)
  - Burst: policy-driven buffer to 32 GPUs (with priority preemption rules)
  - Ramp: 4 -> 12 in month 1, 12 -> 16 in month 2 (customer-controlled rollout)
  - Est. committed cost: $72,000/mo; autoscaling add-on +$5,800/mo

- Option C: Growth (headroom + cost efficiency)
  - Cluster: 64x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs
  - Min guaranteed: 32 GPUs (staggered reservation tiers)
  - Burst: up to 128 GPUs via cross-region capacity with quota gating
  - Ramp: 12 -> 32 over 60 days, 32 -> 64 over next 90 days (phased)
  - Est. committed cost: $255,000/mo; autoscaling add-on +$18,500/mo

Notes and assumptions:
- Prices above are illustrative list estimates and assume model workload similar to demo (avg token length 150, 40 reqs/s peak). We will provide a workload-specific cost model after you share expected qps and prompt lengths.
- Min guaranteed GPUs are billed as reserved capacity; burst is best-effort or on higher-priced burst buckets depending on plan.
- We recommend a 30–90 day pilot under Option A to validate KV cache hit rates and steady-state throughput — we can accelerate or terminate the ramp based on an agreed SLT check at 30 days.

Next steps: Marcus can confirm technical feasibility and any constraints around KV cache warming and split-shard routing given your model sizes. If procurement wants these in a one-page SOW we can produce that within 48 hours.

Cheers,
Ben

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Asha — quick technical clarifications to make the options actionable:

1) Model memory and shard strategy: if you plan to serve a 70B decoder-only model quantized to 4-bit with a 64k context window, our recommendation shifts upward by ~20% in GPU RAM headroom; Option B should be 20% larger in that case (we'd move to ~20 GPUs reserved). Please confirm model artifact size and quantization target.

2) KV cache warm-up: initial 48–72 hours of traffic will show a cache miss tail. For predictable latency we suggest prewarming with a sample of production prompts (we can run a short replay during pilot). Prewarm increases transient GPU utilization but reduces token cost afterward.

3) Autoscaling and minimum billing granularity: reserved min is enforced at 1-hour granularity for billing. Burst pools are metered separately and priced at higher per-GPU rates.

I'll attach a short tech note (inline) and can sketch a concrete ramp playbook once we have expected QPS and model shape.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Patel <asha@pegasusbio.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@pegasusbio.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - initial sizing ask

Thanks Ben and Marcus — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and infra: 

- Procurement: can you show committed vs on-demand delta per month in a simple table? They want to understand the pure cash impact if we increase committed GPUs vs using on-demand solely for production.
- Infra: we plan to serve a 12B ensemble (two models, each ~24GB FP16 in memory) with quantized endpoints. So Marcus's guidance on memory headroom applies but is less aggressive than the 70B case.
- Pilot ask: procurement prefers a 6-week pilot that guarantees 2 reserved GPUs and burst to 8. After pilot they will decide between Option A (scaled) or Option B. They also asked for SOW and a high-level SLA (uptime + latency SLO).

Can you confirm whether the 6-week pilot can be converted into a credit toward committed capacity if we convert to Option B within 30 days of pilot end? Also please include (in the SOW) a clause on data separation and audit log retention (30/90/365 options).

Thanks — Asha
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@pegasusbio.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@pegasusbio.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - initial sizing ask

Asha — all good. Quick confirmations and proposed contractual mechanics below: 

1) Committed vs on-demand delta: we will produce a 1-page table comparing committed monthly cost vs running equivalent capacity on on-demand (example snapshot attached). Rough rule of thumb is committed saves ~20–35% vs sustained on-demand depending on burst use. We'll send the table with your SOW within 24 hours.

2) Pilot conversion credit: yes — standard offer is to credit up to 100% of pilot committed spend toward an annual reserved commitment if you elect to convert within 30 days of pilot completion. We will show the credit as a line item in the SOW.

3) Pilot terms we propose for procurement acceptance:
   - Length: 6 weeks (42 days)
   - Reserved: 2 GPUs guaranteed, burst to 8 GPUs
   - Success review at day 30 with pre-agreed SLT checks (avg latency, error rate, KV cache hit rate)
   - Conversion credit: pilot committed spend credited pro rata to first year committed invoice if Option B selected within 30 days of pilot end

4) SOW items: we will include data separation controls, audit log retention options (30/90/365 days), encryption-at-rest and in-transit, and an SLA section (uptime target + latency SLOs by percentile).

5) Proposed phased ramp (if moving to Option B after pilot):
   - Week 0 (post-conversion): 4 reserved GPUs (staggered activation)
   - Month 1: 4 -> 12 reserved GPUs (two-week increments)
   - Month 2: 12 -> 16 reserved GPUs
   - Hot-standby burst to 32 GPUs for traffic spikes (policy-controlled)

Attachments: proposed_terms.pdf (one-page commitment summary), pilot_scope.docx (pilot success criteria).

Next step: I'll have legal and your procurement exchange a draft SOW/contract with the credit clause — happy to put a conference call on Thursday to walk procurement through the SOW.

Best,
Ben
